verified.location: SI Sec. 8 C, Table 4 (p. 9), row L = 8, column 'Energy per site HFDS (PBC-OBC)' (PNAS journal SI); arXiv v2 Table IV prints -0.7309(6) in this cell
verified.note: Energy verified against the journal; sigma differs (ambiguous entry). Version difference: v2 printed -0.7309(6), the metastable half-filled-stripe state ('S = 0 or small values of S lead to a half-filled stripe configuration of higher energy'), the journal the lower filled-stripe state ('Larger values of S yield a filled-stripe configuration', main Sec. 3 B, p. 6); the stored value follows the journal and the first author's upload (b71872b, 2022-07-16, after v2 of 18 Jun 2022: -23.520 | 0.001 | 0.035(4)). 4 x 8, n = 7/8 = 14 up + 14 down at zero magnetization, U = 8, t = 1, Eq. 1 with no shift. N~ = 16 and alpha = 14 for L = 8 ('A good trade-off ... is achieved by the addition of N~ = 16 hidden fermions for all system sizes. We also consider a two-layer fully connected neural network of hidden-unit density α = {60, 14, 6} for the L = {4, 8, 16} sizes', main Sec. 3 B, p. 6), lambda = 8 soft mean-field constraint on phi_v ('To guide the wave-function ansatz toward the λ = 8 stripe order, we add a soft mean-field constraint', p. 6): method string and detail right. Variational VMC bound, own computation. 0.0445 above the VarBench DMRG row -23.5645; not the record. M6/M8 settled from the source: a sampled VMC energy ('General expectation values and gradients of the objective function are computed using Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling', main text Sec. 2 C, p. 5) whose stored sigma is the uploader's Monte Carlo error; units.mjs counts the row deterministic only because 'Soft mean-field constraint' matches /mean[- ]field/ (units.mjs line 20), which changes nothing while sigma is stored (isSampled is consulted only when sigma is null). Venue PNAS, peer reviewed ('Edited by Angel Rubio ... received December 6, 2021; accepted June 28, 2022'; 'This article is a PNAS Direct Submission'); the imported row carries no peer_reviewed field (loader-level, see report). No duplicate (the '8x4 cylinder' HFDS row -23.46944 is PRB 113, 245104's own computation).

compute.reported_as: Sec. IV: In the simulations, we fix d = 64, h = 8 and d' = 128. [...] In what follows we fix n_l = 2, N~ = 18 and use a single-determinant in the JBf. [...] In our simulations, all wavefunctions required approximately the same number of steps to reach energy convergence (~5000). Beyond the number of variational parameters and optimization steps, the performance and computational cost is impacted by the number of network evaluations per step, which is proportional to the number of Monte Carlo samples being used, and may increase with certain symmetrization strategies. We also investigate how increasing the number of Monte Carlo samples impacts the accuracy of the converged energy. Specifically, we select the best hyperparameters identified in the previous analysis and re-optimized them using 2048, 4096, 8192 and 16384 samples. || Table I caption (Appendix E): Energies are estimated using 131072 samples. || Acknowledgements: This project was provided with computing HPC and storage resources by GENCI at IDRIS thanks to the grant 2024-A0170515698 on the supercomputer Jean Zay's A100 partition. We acknowledge EuroHPC Joint Undertaking for awarding us access to Leonardo at CINECA, Italy through grant EHPC-AI-2024A05-006.
compute.source: Sec. IV (Results) and IV.B; Appendix E Table I caption; Acknowledgements, arXiv:2510.11710 (compute pass 2026-09-16)
compute.note: ~5000 optimization steps is stated for all 8x4-cylinder wavefunctions (both ansaetze, all symmetrizations). Training sample count for the reported 8x4 energy is not pinned down: the paper re-optimized the best hyperparameters with 2048, 4096, 8192 and 16384 samples (Fig. 3) and Table I does not say which; 131072 samples were used only to evaluate the final energies. Architecture: ViT with d = 64, h = 8 heads, n_l = 2 encoder blocks, d' = 128; HFDS with N~ = 18 hidden fermions, JBf with one determinant; symmetrized over space group x spin parity, |G| = 32. Parameter counts appear only as the x-axis of Fig. 2, no number in text. Hardware only at acknowledgement level (Jean Zay A100 partition, Leonardo at CINECA); no GPU count, GPU-hours or wall-clock stated.
